title: Timeline reconstructor with tenant-aware stageable rollback
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build a timeline reconstructor service that re-computes derived analytics timeseries and console metrics for arbitrary historical windows while providing per-tenant staging environments and a stageable rollback (two-phase commit) so operators can validate outputs before swapping live dashboards. The reconstructor must be idempotent, monotonic with respect to event ordering, cost-aware, and capable of throttled execution to avoid impacting production ingestion or Dedicated cluster capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Can run a tenant-scoped reconstruction for a 7-day window with <1% divergence from a ground truth dry-run after transforms are applied
Generated staging outputs are isolated in tenant staging namespace and can be promoted or rolled back within 10 minutes via the Console UI
Reconstruction jobs are idempotent and resume from checkpoints after operator interruption or worker failures
Cost-estimate and impact preview is shown before job start and respects cluster and quota safeguards
Automated end-to-end test that validates reconstruct -> promote -> rollback for a synthetic tenant data set is included in pipeline-ci
design_notes: We will use an event-sourced hybrid approach: materialize events from the raw event topic(s) into ordered tenant shards, then re-apply transformation graph (same transform code used in ingest) to produce derived aggregates.

Two-phase execution: 1) Dry-run compute into isolated staging tables (namespace: staging/{tenant}/{job_id}) with computed diffs and lightweight sanity checks; 2) If validation passes, atomic promotion via swapping read alias or merge with write-lock to live tables.

Checkpointing: append only job state in control-store (S3+metadata DB) with per-shard resume tokens (event-offset + checksum) to ensure exactly-once semantics for recomputation. Use monotonic logical timestamps to guard against out-of-order applies.
Shard strategy: consistent hashing by tenant -> shard key, with hot-tenant split heuristics. Each shard runs as an independent worker to allow parallelism and fine-grained throttles.

Safety: built-in kill-switch that pauses new promotions and automatically decays staging TTL after 72 hours to avoid stale staged data. Operators can mark jobs as emergency-rollbackable which forces safe-merge semantics needed for critical customer incidents.
Cost control: estimate tokens/rows processed based on historical ingest rate per tenant. Jobs auto-throttle to a budgeted Rs (throughput) and attach cost labeling for chargeback.

Technology choices considered: Apache Flink (stream reprocessing primitives) vs batch Spark runs; we choose a hybrid runner where small windows use streaming replays (low-latency) and long windows use vectorized batch runs for cost efficiency.

Compatibility: must run on both Hosted and Dedicated analytics fleets; expose knobs for region affinity and GPU-less execution in private deployments. Audit logs for every promotion are required for Private customers.

Validation hooks: run our existing console-evals prompt sets to flag regressions in key derived metrics (top-k errors, session-duration drift, feature-flag coverage) and surface changes in Console UI.
Migration path: provide an opt-in beta for a small set of tenants before broad rollout. Use canary promotions to validate on live traffic at low blast radius.
rollout_plan: Week 1: implement control-store schema and per-shard resume token format; add job orchestration API endpoints (POST /reconstruct, GET /reconstruct/{id})
Week 2: implement dry-run compute worker and tenant staging namespace; wire up preview diffs to Console UI
Week 3: implement promotion/rollback APIs and safe-swap mechanism for read alias; add audit logging
Week 4: internal canary with platform team tenants (10 tenants), collect metrics and drift reports
Week 5: opt-in beta customers (30 tenants) with dedicated runbook and SRE on-call support
Post-beta: release flag to all Console orgs with rate limits and cost caps
test_plan: Unit tests for resume-token encoding/decoding and idempotency guards
Integration test: synthetic tenant ingest -> reconstruct -> promote -> rollback cycle in CI (pipeline-ci)
Chaos test: worker termination and control-store corruption simulation to validate resumability
Performance test: run 30-day reconstruction for a medium tenant in staging cluster and measure cost & completion time
Security test: verify KMS usage for staging artifact encryption and audit entries for promotions
